source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Left-sided heart failure alone, with fairly little connection to the client's underlying chronic pulmonary disease","B":"Chronic pulmonary hypertension related to lung disease, leading to right ventricular strain and eventual right-sided heart failure","C":"A condition generally considered entirely unrelated to the client's underlying chronic pulmonary disease process","D":"An improvement in the client's overall right ventricular function as their underlying COPD continues to progress"}}
source_row.rationale: Cor pulmonale results from chronic pulmonary hypertension related to underlying lung disease (such as severe COPD), leading to right ventricular strain and, over time, right-sided heart failure, an important complication to monitor for in clients with significant chronic lung disease.
source_row.source_name: ACC/AHA — Cor Pulmonale in Chronic Lung Disease
